theorem.fixed_context: One ordered type pair (T,T'), one stored 111 state (p,m,n), one post-Lemma10 descendant P'.
theorem.K_graph: All graph-discoverable triples (y,y',z) satisfying the frozen A/B membership, yy' nonedge, and z in Y0' cap N(y) cap N(y').

proof: Equality of the ordered boundary pair (y,y') is an equivalence relation.
Membership and class keys use only graph/state data.
For each valid pair, a canonical common witness z_can can be selected from Y0' cap N(y) cap N(y') using a fixed vertex order.
A naive construction scans at most O(n^3) incidences and emits at most n^2 pair classes, hence is polynomial and uses no extension oracle.

Q2_ANSWER_RELEVANCE_INVARIANT.claim: For fixed y,y', all common-witness triples are answer-relevant together or irrelevant together.
Q2_ANSWER_RELEVANCE_INVARIANT.formal: For z1,z2 in Y0' cap N(y) cap N(y'), (y,y',z1) is answer-relevant iff (y,y',z2) is answer-relevant.
proof: The frozen answer-relevance predicate asks whether there exists an extension c of the fixed P' with c(y),c(y') in {3,4}.
The identity of the chosen common witness z does not occur in that predicate.
Therefore changing only z cannot change answer relevance.

Q3_EXACT_COLOR_PROJECTION_INVARIANT.projection_definition: Pi(y,y')={(gamma,delta) in {3,4}^2 : there exists an extension c of P' with c(y)=gamma and c(y')=delta}.
Q3_EXACT_COLOR_PROJECTION_INVARIANT.claim: Every member of one z-fiber has exactly the same Pi(y,y').
proof: All members of a class have identical ordered boundary vertices y,y'.
The ambient descendant P' is fixed.
The projection is defined only on these boundary coordinates and the existence of global extensions of P'.
The witness coordinate z is not a boundary coordinate and is not conditioned on by the projection.
Thus the projection is preserved by identity, without computing it via an extension oracle.

Q4_CLASS_SUMMARY.summary: (T,T',p,m,n,y,y',z_can) with fixed context references and canonical common-witness certificate.
Q4_CLASS_SUMMARY.size_property: O(1) vertex identifiers relative to the fixed gate context; independent of the number of z witnesses in the class.
Q4_CLASS_SUMMARY.semantic_property: Retains the exact boundary pair, so the exact {3,4}^2 extension projection is preserved by identity rather than approximated.

Q5_CLASS_COUNT.nontriviality: This is a true quotient of raw triples by removal of the z coordinate; it is not merely the observation that raw triples are <= n^3.

Q6_Y0_COMPONENT_SATURATION.claim: If one common witness z belongs to a connected component C of G[Y0'], then y and y' are complete to C; hence every vertex of C is a common witness.
proof: y,y' lie in descendant Y', hence outside Y0' union X0'.
Descendant axiom (iv) forbids any such vertex from being mixed on an edge of Y0'.
Along a path in a connected component C of G[Y0'], adjacency to y cannot switch from present to absent; likewise for y'.
Since both are adjacent to z in C, both are complete to C.

relation_to_frozen_F3.interpretation: This theorem supplies a valid F3 witness if the family-gate execution reaches F3 after checking the stronger frozen outcomes F1 and F2.

remaining_unknown.possible_multiplicity: up to Theta(n^2) is not ruled out
